\note{Supplementary Note 1. Decision rules}

Every model emits, for DR, four logits whose sigmoids estimate $P(y>k)$, $k=0,\dots,3$
(cumulative head and CORAL), or conditional probabilities $P(y>k\mid y>k-1)$ that are
chained by cumulative product (CORN). From these the expected grade
$s=\sum_k P(y>k)$ is computed. The five rules are:

\begin{description}
\item[R1 (shipped).] Grade $=\#\{k: P(y>k)>0.5\}$ after enforcing monotonicity by a running
minimum. This is what the trained model outputs if deployed unchanged.
\item[R2 (development QWK cut-points).] Four ordered cut-points on $s$ chosen to maximise
QWK on the development out-of-fold predictions, by coordinate ascent over a grid of 60
candidate values per cut-point (8 rounds), then applied unchanged externally.
\item[R3 (R2 with a referral constraint).] R2 with the grade-1/2 cut-point replaced by the
largest value that keeps development referable-DR sensitivity at or above 0.90, the
neighbouring cut-points pushed to preserve order.
\item[R4 and R4m (external, diagnostic).] The same search on the external labels, with the
external set split at random into two halves (seed 0); cut-points fitted on one half are
applied to the other and vice versa, so no image is graded by cut-points fitted on its own
label. R4 maximises QWK, R4m macro-averaged recall. The grid has 80 candidate values.
\end{description}

R4/R4m use external labels and are never reported as performance: they bound what a local
recalibration of the decision rule alone, without retraining, can recover. Changing the
development grid from 60 to 80 values changes E08's matched development QWK by
\pn{grid.effect}; 60 is used for all development quantities because it reproduces the archived
matched comparisons exactly.

%% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\note{Supplementary Note 2. The DME grade cannot be derived from published lesion masks}

IDRiD defines its DME risk grade by the distance from the fovea to the nearest hard exudate:
grade 0, no exudate; grade 1, exudates more than one disc diameter from the fovea; grade 2,
within one disc diameter. Because the definition is geometric, a grade derived from the
pixel-level hard-exudate masks that IDRiD releases for 81 images, together with its
fovea and optic-disc annotations, should reproduce the expert grade if the grade is what its
definition says. The protocol was pre-registered (\texttt{docs/PARTA\_preregistration.md}).

Of the 81 segmentation images, \pn{parta.n} could be linked to their grading-set copies by
pixel correlation (minimum correlation 0.9999). The disc diameter was measured from the
optic-disc mask in three ways (major axis, minor axis, equivalent-area diameter); all three
give the same grades. The derived grade matched the expert grade in \pn{parta.exact}\% of
images, against \pn{parta.constant}\% for a constant predictor, because almost every
segmentation image is grade 2. On the \pn{parta.informative} images where the test is
informative (expert grade 0 or 1), the derivation failed twice: an image graded 1 whose
nearest exudate lies 53 pixels from the fovea (disc diameter 612 pixels), and an image graded
0 with a single exudate 87 pixels from the fovea (disc diameter 657 pixels). In both, a single
small exudate inside the threshold is either not counted by the grader or not visible at
grading resolution. The pre-registered gate (exact agreement above the constant predictor on
the informative images) therefore failed, and no derived DME labels were used anywhere.

\note{Supplementary Note 3. A per-grade verdict that depends on the cut-point procedure}

The development record that motivated the matched-calibration rule included a source control
(E12): two runs identical except for whether Messidor-2 images came from the default or the
native-resolution files, compared on the 953 development images both could use. Moderate
recall, native minus default, under four ways of setting both arms' cut-points:

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lc@{}}
\toprule
Cut-points for both arms & Moderate recall difference (points) [95\% CI] \\
\midrule
Shipped (0.5) & \pn{rec.e12.shipped} \pn{rec.e12.shippedci} \\
Fitted on all rows (in-sample) & \pn{rec.e12.insample} \pn{rec.e12.insampleci} \\
Random two-fold cross-fit, grid 80 & \pn{rec.e12.randomhalf} \pn{rec.e12.randomhalfci} \\
Fold-wise cross-fit, grid 60 (development standard) & \pn{rec.e12.matched} \pn{rec.e12.matchedci} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The originally archived value, which the project had cited as the case in which a difference
\emph{survived} matched calibration, is reproduced by the random-half procedure; under the
fold-wise procedure used for every other development comparison it dissolves. Aggregate QWK
is indistinguishable under every procedure. Two consequences are drawn in the main text: a
matched-calibration claim must name its fitting procedure, and per-grade claims should be
reported under at least two. The two-directional property of the rule (that it can confirm
as well as dissolve a difference) rests instead on EfficientNet-B3 versus the 560-pixel
DenseNet121, which survives matched calibration on the development pool
(\pn{iv.effnet.ship} shipped, \pn{iv.effnet.diff} \pn{iv.effnet.ci} matched), and on
per-grade external differences that stay significant at every rule (Table~3 of the main
text).

\note{Supplementary Note 4. Correction of an archived ordinal-head comparison}

Regenerating every development number from the archived per-image logits with independent
code reproduced each archived matched QWK exactly except one. The archived comparison of the
CORN head against the reference reported \pn{corn.archived.diff} \pn{corn.archived.ci}, a
significant deficit, with matched QWK \pn{corn.archived.qwk} for CORN. The archived script had
decoded CORN's conditional logits as if they were cumulative; decoding them by cumulative
product, as the training code does, gives matched QWK \pn{dev.e22corn.matched} and a
difference of \pn{iv.corn.diff} \pn{iv.corn.ci}, indistinguishable from the reference. The
pre-registered verdict (no improvement) is unchanged; the claim that CORN is worse, and the
mechanism once offered for it, are withdrawn. The script was corrected to read each run's
head from its results file (repository \texttt{ISSUES.md}, \S30).

\note{Supplementary Note 5. Seed variation (O1--O3)}

The reference configuration was trained with \pn{seeds.n} different seeds on identical data,
split and recipe. Matched development QWK ranged \pn{seeds.dev.lo}--\pn{seeds.dev.hi} (s.d.\
\pn{seeds.dev.sd}); the yardstick for a difference beyond seed noise between two
configurations is therefore $2\sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{s.d.}=\pn{seeds.yardstick}$ (grey band in
Fig.~6). On APTOS under the shipped rule, QWK ranged \pn{seeds.aptos.qwklo}--\pn{seeds.aptos.qwkhi}
(s.d.\ \pn{seeds.aptos.sd}). Of \pn{seeds.aptos.ntests} per-grade recall differences between
pairs of seeds, \pn{seeds.aptos.sigR1} had a bootstrap interval excluding zero under R1 (largest
absolute difference \pn{seeds.aptos.maxR1} points) and \pn{seeds.aptos.sigR4} under R4: the
pre-registered prediction O2 that seeds alone produce more than five ``significant''
per-grade differences \pn{seeds.o2}. Mild recall under the shipped rule was
\pn{seeds.aptos.mildR1.lo}--\pn{seeds.aptos.mildR1.hi}\% and under R4m
\pn{seeds.aptos.mildR4m.lo}--\pn{seeds.aptos.mildR4m.hi}\% in every seed (O3 \pn{seeds.o3}).

\note{Supplementary Note 6. Reverse direction (O4--O6)}

To test whether the mild-grade collapse is specific to transfer from the development pool,
the reference recipe was trained on APTOS 2019 (its own frozen 5-fold split, near-duplicates
grouped) and evaluated on Messidor-2 and IDRiD, the direction in which a published
ordinal-regression model was reported to lose the mild grade. Matched out-of-fold QWK on
APTOS was \pn{rev.dev.qwk}. On Messidor-2 under the shipped rule mild recall was
\pn{rev.m2.R1.mild}\% (O4 \pn{rev.o4}); external cut-points (R4m) raised it to
\pn{rev.m2.R4m.mild}\% without retraining (O5 \pn{rev.o5}). The mean predicted minus true
grade under the shipped rule was \pn{rev.m2.R1.mean} (O6, under-grading in the reverse
direction, \pn{rev.o6}).

\note{Supplementary Note 7. Content-overlap audit}

Public fundus corpora are assembled from overlapping sources, so a near-duplicate of an
external image in the training data would inflate external performance. Every image of the
development pool, APTOS, DDR and EyePACS was reduced to a 256-bit difference hash after the
same retinal crop used for training, and all cross-corpus pairs within \pn{ov.bits} bits were
counted (in this project's data, distinct images lie at least 28 bits apart and re-encodings of
one image within 8). The development pool and the frozen split were built before this audit;
development near-duplicate pairs that straddle two folds number \pn{ov.crossfold}.

\input{supp/table_s8.tex}
